text:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy of service inference-v2 to eu-west-1 failed health checks. Automated rollback was initiated but rollout-orchestrator state is 'rollback_pending' and some hooks are blocking. deploy_id=deploy_2026_05_03_17:54

incident-bot: @oncall paging SRE — elevated 5xx rate on inference-v2 canary in eu-west-1. Observed 503 spikes. Potential customer impact. Dashboard: <https://dash.internal/redwood/inference-v2?window=15m>

maria: i'm on it. looking at the deploy logs and pods. can someone confirm we didn't run any DB migrations in this canary?

jess: correct — no migrations. just model artifact + config flip. flipped ff.inference.v2.canary -> true for 10% traffic.

kai: kubectl shows rollout stuck: replicaset scaling down, but pods are stuck Terminating. postStop hook appears to be waiting. pods show TERM_WAIT.

omri: DB side: I see long-running sessions holding an advisory lock:

```
SELECT pid, state, query
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE state = 'active' AND query LIKE '%advisory_lock%';
```

pid 54321 is active with query 'select pg_sleep(300)'. That is preventing locks from clearing.

jess: that matches: we added a preload that uses pg_advisory_lock to avoid stampede when loading embeddings. it should release on exit but looks like SIGTERM didn't trigger cleanup.

maria: so pods can't finish postStop because preload job is holding the lock -> pod termination blocks -> rollback can't progress. makes sense.

kai: options: (1) kill the DB session (fast) (2) force-delete pods (kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 --force) (3) attempt manual rollback creation bypassing termination waits (risky)

leah: support: customers reporting 503s since 17:53 UTC. Affected: partner-qa, trial-org-53. Impact estimate ~12% of traffic for eu-west-1.

dan: product: if impact >10% we should open an incident bridge and start customer comms. i'm prepping a short note.

maria: i'll do option 1. @omri can you identify host and drop the pid? need to clear lock ASAP.

omri: identified session on pg-euw-2, pid 54321, application_name=inference-preload. killing now.

[system] omri killed pid 54321

omri: locks cleared.

deploy-bot: Orchestrator observed lock release. postStop hooks proceeding, pods are now terminating and replicaset scaling down. Rollback resuming.

kai: scaling down old RS and bringing up previous stable RS. watching for readiness probes.

jess: starting verification: smoke tests for generate, embeddings, and lookup flows. running scripts: `scripts/smoke/inference_smoke.sh`

maria: quick handoff: i have 20m left on shift. @kai you'll take over after smoke is green.

kai: taking over. will monitor metrics and traces, specifically tail latencies and error rate.

leah: support update: sending templated message to affected customers explaining rollback and that we are monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident bridge created: https://bridge.redwood/incident/IR-2026-0423-78 (owner: maria -> kai after handoff)

maria: smoke tests: 5/5 generates ok, embeddings 10/10, health endpoints return 200.

kai: metrics: error rate in eu-west-1 down from ~12% to ~0.5%. request latency back to baseline.

jess: root cause: preload job didn't handle SIGTERM properly and held advisory locks. PR to fix: #1458 (add SIGTERM handler, bounded retry, shorter lock durations).

dan: scheduling postmortem. severity: SEV2. action items: update runbook to cover blocking postStop hooks, add guardrails on startup locks, and add a short postStop timeout in deployment config.

maria: i'll file a quick runbook note with the commands we used (kill pid, force checks) and include links to the PR.

[automated note] summary: rollback completed at 2026-05-03T18:06:20Z. Impact: elevated 5xx in eu-west-1 (~12% of requests), customers impacted: partner-qa, trial-org-53. Root cause: preload process holding DB advisory locks preventing pod termination and blocking orchestrator rollback. Actions: PR #1458, runbook update, improve postStop timeout and SIGTERM handling, customer communications sent.

kai: tagging follow-ups: @jess @omri @dan. closing thread unless new alerts appear.
